pr_body:
Toggling 'editable_children' off in the SceneTree will now no longer result in nodes owned by the currently edited scene, but assigned as children of foreign nodes, from being accidentally lost, where they before would still be visible in the scene, but not viewable since their parents were made hidden. They will instead be moved to the root of the instance, with their global transform perserved in the case of Node2D and Node3D derivatives. The editable children toggle will now also be subject to functional undoing and redoing.

Closes #46726
pr_comments: Okay, this has been updated with the reparent function. Would recommend a new review since this bug is still relevant and still a bad UX trap.

Okay, I've made a bunch of updates and corrected most of what @KoBeWi pointed out. A lot of the issues were holdovers from the initial PR and I've corrected them now. There's a couple of points I've provided explanations for why its done that way though.

Something went wrong:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/2223172/cd3b0145-c56b-4423-9607-9384f253a153
```
Can't add child 'A' to itself.
Invalid owner. Owner must be an ancestor in the tree
```

Okay, sorry, I think I've fixed this *properly* this time.
- Fixed main node disappearing when removing editable children
- Made it so that update_all_gizmos method is binded properly and put it back seperately in the UndoRedo action to prevent the editable children status not correctly updating.
- Removed the empty method defintion.
Changed PR and commit title to better match preferred submission format.
Rebased and amended to apply @AThousandShips' suggestions.

After this was merged I have started getting errors like:
`scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp:1648 - Index p_idx = 6 is out of bounds (nodes.size() = 3).`
spammed in the editor output whenever I save a scene containing an instanced child scene that is inherited and 'editable_children' is enabled. If 'editable_children' is disabled I don't have any issue.

See #87424

issue_context.title: A node instanced as a child of a foreign node doesn't get saved after Editable Children is unchecked.
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues for potential duplicates before filing yours:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues?q=is%3Aissue
-->

**Godot version:**
<!-- Specify commit hash if using non-official build. -->
f477d3ca9851953ded5f0560081d726f5de9b534, master (8faecd6a470aeef41084a32d74f4a131a5ef42b6)


**OS/device including version:**
<!-- Specify GPU model, drivers, and the backend (GLES2, GLES3, Vulkan) if graphics-related. -->
Windows 7 SP1


**Issue description:**
<!-- What happened, and what was expected. -->
After unchecking "Editable Children" i expected a node added as a child of a foreign node to either
- survive saving and reopening a scene
- be removed when "Editable Children" becomes unchecked.

Since users really don't like loosing their work it's probably better to go with the first option.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Disable Editable Children of "Node2D"

2. Click on Godot logo

3. "Sprite" will get selected and will be editable in the inspector while not visible in Scene dock

4. Save the scene and reopen it. "Sprite" node will be gone.

**Minimal reproduction project:**
<!-- A small Godot project which reproduces the issue. Drag and drop a zip archive to upload it. -->
https://github.com/hilfazer/Projects/tree/EngineIssues/Godot/EngineIssues/ChildrenOfForeignNodes_godot32
https://github.com/hilfazer/Projects/tree/EngineIssues/Godot/EngineIssues/ChildrenOfForeignNodes_godot40
and open SelectSprite.tscn

review_comments: This looks like it should be in `else` of the condition below?

So I'm a little confused what you mean. The if statement is basically meant to check if the nodes in the array are parented to nodes owned by the instance we just removed editable children status from.

Admitedly though, after looking over it, I think this was the wrong place to put it. Instead, I've put it up in _toggle_editable_children when constructing the initial arrays, because otherwise, there's discontinuity between the two methods and this check doesn't reflect the description of what this specific method is meant to do.

What I meant was that `reparent()` clears the owner, so setting it before reparenting is pointless (you are still doing it). 

Previously your reparenting was conditional, so the unconditional `set_owner()` should go under `else` of that condition. This part is no longer relevant.

Although after second look, `node` is not part of the `owned` (I think?), so the `node->set_owner()` should still be done after somewhere after reparenting.

I think this method and the one below could be merged. You don't need transform and name arrays, as noted in comments above, and paths can be empty when reparenting to root. Though maybe I'm missing something.

While it seems overkill, I can explain why we have the names and transforms array. For explanation of names, see the explanation to the above response about undoing naming conflicts. As for the transforms, while its uncommon given a revert chain should put things back to its relative position before the reparent, storing the original transforms will restore it in situations where the local position might change. In example I was testing, I had a scene with an animated skeleton and bone attachments. If I instance this scene in another scene, make it editable, then attach a mesh to that bone attachment, then remove the editable status, the mesh will become detached. This is fine, but if the skeleton is animating, upon undoing the action to remove the editable children status, we don't know how to restore it local position by just using reparenting, hence the use of the transform array.

Admittedly, yeah, it this wasn't doing anything because the code to restore the local transform got lost during the migration to the reparent function, but I've restored it now.
You could store the previous name in a variable right before reparent. No need to keep it in Array I think.

Actually, I looked over this one, and no, the reason we keep it in an array is to revert naming conflicts. In the incident, that the node gets reparented to another node when its owner has its editable status removed, it may conflict with a matching name. By storing the names in an array, it means it can correctly restore its original name upon undoing.
